name: a_rates_fed
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Rates & Fed.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
2-yr, 10-yr, 30-yr Treasury yields (level, bp change); Treasury auction results (high yield, bid-to-cover, tail); CME FedWatch probabilities for the next FOMC; every Fed official who spoke, with verbatim quotes.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Rates & Fed `[Macro]`

- **2-year Treasury yield:** 4.808%, up 1.1 bp on Thursday, October 15; session high was 4.952%. The latest cited reading before the cutoff was 4.808% (Exante, Oct 15, time not stated).[7]
- **10-year Treasury yield:** 5.186%, down 3.7 bp on Thursday, October 15; session high was 5.329%. The Treasury daily par-curve reading at approximately 15:30 ET was 5.10%, down 9 bp from October 14 (Exante, Oct 15, time not stated; EconoTimes, Oct 16, time not stated).[2][7]
- **30-year Treasury yield:** 5.525%, down 3.8 bp on Thursday, October 15; session high was 5.628%. The Treasury daily par-curve reading at approximately 15:30 ET was 5.48%, down 9 bp from October 14 (Exante, Oct 15, time not stated; EconoTimes, Oct 16, time not stated).[2][7]
- **CME FedWatch:** The implied probability of an October 27–28 rate increase was 27.1%; the probability that the December target would be at least 25 bp above the current target was 86.3% (Exante, Oct 15, time not stated).[7]
- **Mary Daly, San Francisco Fed president:** “We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we’re still deliberating”; she also said, “I don’t feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information” (Reuters interview published Oct 15; republished by bdnews24 at 10:44 ET).[6]
- **Mary Daly:** “Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated,” but “risks are not realities,” and “reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent” (Reuters interview published Oct 15; republished by bdnews24 at 10:44 ET).[6]
- **Mary Daly:** “Why force urgency when you don’t need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? And we have more meetings ahead of us” (Reuters interview published Oct 15; republished by bdnews24 at 10:44 ET).[6]
- **Beth Hammack, Cleveland Fed president:** “What I worry about is, if you get this inflationary mindset, if you get these expectations that these price pressures become more and more persistent, it makes it much harder for monetary policy to do the work that we need to do, and we might need to move even more than if you don't have an inflationary mindset set in” (Reuters, Oct 15, time not stated).[1]
- **Beth Hammack:** “I’m not feeling that there’s restraint coming from financial conditions at this…point in time” (Reuters, Oct 15, time not stated).[1]
- **John Williams, New York Fed president:** “I haven’t changed my view that it may be appropriate to have one more rate hike” this year; he added, “I don’t think at this time I have any reason to believe that we would need to do more” after that (Bloomberg interview reported by Reuters and republished by The Star, Oct 15, time not stated).[3]
- **John Williams:** He estimated the real neutral rate at 1% “or a little above that” (Bloomberg interview reported by Reuters and republished by The Star, Oct 15, time not stated).[3]
- **Austan Goolsbee, Chicago Fed president:** A Reuters events listing identified Goolsbee as scheduled to speak on October 15; no quote or speech text was included in the available result (Reuters, Oct 15, time not stated).[9]
- **Kevin Warsh, Fed chair:** Reuters identified a speech scheduled for early October 16 at an IMF meeting in Bangkok; no quote or speech text published by the cutoff was included in the available result (Reuters, Oct 15, time not stated).[1][9]
- **4-week Treasury bill auction:** Bid-to-cover was 2.56 versus 2.40 previously; the stop-out yield was 4.00% versus 3.98% previously (XTB, Oct 15, time not stated).[4]
- **3-year Treasury note auction:** High yield was 4.932%, bid-to-cover was 2.62x, and indirect bidders received 57.6% (Au79 Macro Research, Oct 14, outside the requested publication window; background only).[8]
- **10-year Treasury note auction:** High yield was 5.300%, bid-to-cover was 2.77x, and indirect bidders received 80.3% (Au79 Macro Research, Oct 14, outside the requested publication window; background only).[8]
- **30-year Treasury bond auction:** High yield was 5.618%, bid-to-cover was 2.54x, and indirect bidders received 72.3% (Au79 Macro Research, Oct 14, outside the requested publication window; background only).[8]
